items.title: TCS Hits $1.5B AI Revenue | ChatGPT App Store is HERE | G42 NANDA & India Funding Report
items.summary: In this episode of Front Page, we dive into the pivotal shift in the AI landscape as OpenAI officially kicks off the "Platform Era" with the launch of the ChatGPT App Directory, effectively transforming the tool into an AI operating system for developers and creators. We also break down major enterprise moves as TCS pivots to an AI-first model, disclosing a massive $1.5 billion annualized AI revenue run rate across 5,500+ projects. On the innovation front, we discuss G42’s release of NANDA 87B, a breakthrough Hindi-English open-weight model, and are joined by G42 India CEO Manu Kumar Jain to explore what this means for sovereign AI in the Global South. Finally, we decode the resilience of India's startup ecosystem—which raised $10.5 billion in 2025 despite global headwinds—with special guest Neha Singh, co-founder of Tracxn, who analyzes the surge in IPOs and market maturity.

items.title: The ChatGPT App Store is HERE: OpenAI’s Massive Platform Shift
items.summary:
OpenAI has officially crossed a historic milestone with the launch of the ChatGPT App Directory and a new Apps SDK, marking the end of ChatGPT as just a chatbot and the beginning of its era as a fully integrated platform. This update allows third-party services to live directly inside conversations, meaning users can now browse, search, and trigger real-world actions—like ordering food via Zomato, deploying code with Replit, or building full-stack apps with Lovable—without ever leaving the chat interface. In this episode of Front Page, we break down why this move from "connectors" to native apps is a massive shift in software economics, effectively positioning ChatGPT as the new operating layer for the internet where intent drives action. We also analyze what this means for developers looking for distribution, how it mirrors the early days of the Apple App Store, and why the future of software is no longer about fighting for screen space, but fighting for agent access.


This is Front Page, your daily decode of the battles shaping the future of AI, compute, and human intent. No noise. No hype. Just the signal that matters.

items.title: Will AI Kill Indian IT? TCS Just Gave the Answer
items.summary:
India’s largest IT services company just made its clearest AI statement yet. For the first time ever, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has officially broken out its AI numbers, and they are massive. With $1.5 Billion in annual AI revenue and over 5,500 AI projects live globally, TCS is no longer just "experimenting" with Artificial Intelligence.
But the real story isn't just the money. It's the mindset shift. In a move that stunned analysts, TCS CEO K Krithivasan declared an "AI-First" culture—even if it means cannibalising their own revenue to stay ahead. From automating 280,000 hackathon entries to building their own "HyperVault" infrastructure, TCS is aggressively pivoting from a service provider to a strategic AI partner.

In this video, we analyze:
The Numbers: Breaking down the $1.5B revenue and 16.3% growth.
The Culture Shift: Why TCS is willing to automate its own billable hours.
The Moat: How they used AI to do 12 months of work in just 3 weeks.
The Risk: Can TCS survive the transition from "Headcount" to "Outcome"?
The Competition: How does this stack up against Accenture and other global giants?
Is this the moment Indian IT finally evolves?


Let us know in the comments: Do you think AI will shrink the Indian IT workforce or make it more valuable?

items.title: 87 Billion Parameters! Is NANDA the Most Powerful Hindi AI Yet?
items.summary:
One of the biggest names in Indian tech is back—and this time, he's building the brain of India's AI future. In this exclusive episode of Front Page, we are joined by Manu Kumar Jain (CEO, G42 India) to break down G42's massive new launch: NANDA 87B.

This isn't just another chatbot. NANDA 87B is an open-weight, 87-billion-parameter language model trained specifically for Hindi, English, and the way Indians actually speak—Hinglish. 🇮🇳 Trained on the super-powerful Condor Galaxy with Cerebras, this model is designed to bridge the gap between global benchmarks and real-world Indian utility.

In this deep dive, Manu opens up about: 
The Launch: Why G42 built a population-scale model for India. 
The Language Gap: Solving the "Hinglish" problem that US models ignore. 
Open Source: Why releasing open weights is critical for the Global South. 
The Bigger Vision: From smartphones (Xiaomi) to Sovereign AI—Manu's new mission.


Is India ready to move from consuming AI to building its own AI infrastructure?

👇Let us know in the comments: Do you think a Hindi-first model will change how we use the internet in India?

items.title: India Ranks 3rd Globally in Tech Funding | Tracxn Annual Report 2025
items.summary:
India has successfully defied the global capital crunch to rank as the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem, raising $10.5 billion in 2025—trailing only the US and UK. In this episode of Front Page, we sit down with Neha Singh, Co-Founder of Tracxn, to break down the India Tech Annual Funding Report 2025 and uncover the reality behind the numbers. While headline funding has dipped by 17%, the ecosystem is signaling a massive structural shift toward maturity, evidenced by a surge in IPOs, resilient early-stage growth, and continued investor confidence in sectors like FinTech and Enterprise. Join us as we decode the "seed-stage squeeze," the dominance of Bengaluru, and why the data suggests India is moving away from unicorn obsession toward disciplined, high-value exits.

Build Your Own AI Agent in Minutes with h2oGPTe
items.summary:
In this session, Andreea, Head of Training @H2Oai , walks through how to build a fully functional AI agent in minutes using Enterprise h2oGPTe from a simple prompt to a smart, policy-aware agent that generates structured outputs and even powers an interactive dashboard.

This hands-on demo uses a real-world example: creating policy-compliant holiday gift recommendations based on company guidelines.

⸻

🔗 Demo & Resources Used in This Session

⤷ Live Agent Demo (GitHub Pages):
https://andreea-turcu.github.io/holiday-company-gift-card-agents-demo/

⤷ Company Policy Document (RAG Example – v1):
https://triagelogic.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/Company-Policy-and-Procedure-June-1.18-V6.0.pdf

⤷ Company Policy Document with Gift-Giving Guidelines (v2):
https://diabengineering.com.au/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/HSE-MAN-001-001-DIAB-Engineering-Policy-Manual-Rev05-All-Policies.pdf

⸻

⤷ Example Prompt Used in the Demo

I need to find appropriate holiday gifts for 3 different people:
 1. A colleague who loves tech gadgets (budget $40–70)
 2. A senior client who wants thoughtful, professional gifts (budget $80–120)
 3. A new team member who enjoys cooking and creative hobbies (budget $25–50)

Please:
 • Use my company policy guidelines from our RAG collection
 • Follow the budget rules strictly
 • For each person, give 3 gift options
 • Include JSON output with:
 • gift_name
 • price
 • category
 • reason
 • policy_alignment

Make sure recommendations do not violate any company rules, If there are no Gift-Giving Guidelines in this document, please let me know, I will provide to you another updated one.

⸻

⤷ Get Started with h2oGPTe

 • Visit H2O.ai official website : https://h2o.ai/

items.summary:

We can only achieve better system performance, Alex says, when we build tools that keep step with the way that people make decisions. Listen to the episode to hear Alex talk about how he is helping make AI agents work for individuals rather than the companies that develop them, and his work in making sure that systems operate consistently and fairly across the world.

items.title: When will quantum computers beat classical computers?
items.summary:
Explore the podcast → www.ibm.com/think/podcast/the-coherence-times 

Quantum computers have the potential to solve some valuable scientific problems faster, more accurately, or more cost-effectively than any classical computer. They haven't reached this point yet, but when they do, they will have achieved what we call "quantum advantage," a long sought scientific and engineering milestone that will mark the beginning of an exciting new era of computation. So, when will quantum advantage arrive? What methods are researchers and developers to enable their search for advantage? How will we know when it gets here? In this episode of The Coherence Times, we sit down with IBM Principal Research Scientist Abhinav Kandala to discover how, and when, quantum computers will beat classical computers.  

00:00 - Introduction 
4:37 - What is quantum advantage? 
22:38 - How do we look for quantum advantage 
26:48 - How close are we to quantum advantage?

items.title: Google’s $12 Million India AI Push Includes $50K Grant For CoRover.AI | Exclusive -Ankush Sabharwal
items.summary:
Global Big Tech’s battle for India has shifted gears, with Google announcing a massive $12 million commitment to fuel the nation’s AI ecosystem, a move distinct from the infrastructure-heavy plays of Microsoft and Amazon. At its 'Lab to Impact' dialogue, Google revealed a strategy deeply integrated with India’s public systems, funding everything from 'MedGemma' for healthcare foundation models to AI Centres of Excellence at top IITs and IISc. This initiative goes beyond mere code; it includes a critical $4.5 million grant to Wadhwani AI for empowering frontline health and agriculture workers, a new Indic Language hub at IIT Bombay, and a 150 MW solar partnership with ReNew to ensure this digital growth is sustainable. This is Google betting not just on Indian startups, but on the foundational AI layers that will run the country’s health, education, and energy sectors for decades to come.

items.title: From Mylapore to the World: The Story of India’s Sanskrit LLM
items.summary:
India’s first native Sanskrit Large Language Model is being built in the heart of Chennai, marking a historic collaboration between the 118-year-old MDS Sanskrit College in Mylapore and the tech innovators at IIT Madras. This ambitious project goes far beyond simple translation or OCR; it aims to teach Artificial Intelligence the complex logic, "Sandhi," and structure of the world's oldest language by processing over 110,000 rare manuscripts held in local archives. By combining the deep scholarly traditions of institutions like the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute with modern data science, Chennai is positioning itself as the birthplace of India’s digital heritage infrastructure, ensuring that civilizational memory is not just preserved, but actively computed for the future.

items.title: EXL's 25-Year AI Transformation: Chief AI Officer, Andy Logani, on Making Data Real
items.summary:
Join us for an exclusive interview with Andy Logani, Executive Vice President and Chief Digital and AI Officer at EXL, a global data and AI company. Andy details EXL's incredible 25-year journey from a business process operations company to a data and AI powerhouse, with 55% of its revenue now stemming from Data and AI.

The EXL Transformation Journey: Andy reveals the five strategic "tranches" that drove this evolution, including the pivotal 2006 acquisition of Inductus and the subsequent recognition that data, not just technology, was the key to enterprise transformation. This led to strategic acquisitions (Clairvoyant, ITI, RTM) and a powerful foundation that allowed EXL to rapidly embrace the GPT moment.

items.title: The Social Nature of Acquiring Knowledge
items.summary:
In episode 949 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Alex Pentland discusses the reality of human learning, noting that people rarely read manuals. He references Nobel Prize economist Daniel Kahneman's estimate that 95% of human behavior is derived from observing others and the surrounding culture rather than explicit instructions. Pentland explains that questioning peers and observing established cultural norms is the primary method people use to acquire new
skills.
